- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast after a dip, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or mean.
- In cases where true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% over 3–5 days, model may be under-reacting to sentiment; increase forecast slope or lag correction.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift early.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period price if sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.5% buffer for final 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillations, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing or trend-adjusted correction.
